summary: Muhammad Ashraf Khan is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He has served as Director at the Department of Archaeology and Museums (Government of Andhra Pradesh), Deputy Director at Taxila Museum, and Director at Quaid-i-Azam University (attested 2019).

Mumon Yamada (1900–1988) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Hanazono University. He later served as president of Hanazono University around 1949 to 1978 and taught Chung-yuan Chang.

Mun-keat Choong is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Paramadhamma Buddhist Institute (1982) and Komazawa University (BA ~1986–1990). He completed an MA (~1991–1994) supervised by Roderick S. Bucknell and a PhD (~1994–1998) at the University of Queensland.

Munenobu Sakurai (born 1961) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University around 1984–1990. He served as assistant professor at Iwate University (~1993–2002) and became a professor at Tohoku University around 2002.

Muneo Tokunaga (1945–2016) was an Indology scholar who earned degrees from Kyoto University (~1969–1971) and Harvard University (PhD ~1974–1979). He taught at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1981–1989) and served as assistant professor (~1989–1997) and professor (~1997–2009) at Kyoto University.
Mungunchimeg Batmunkh is a scholar of religious studies and Tibetology. Batmunkh earned a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna (attested 2010), studying under doctoral supervisor Brigitte Marschall.

Murray Barnson Emeneau (1904–2005) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Dalhousie University, Balliol College, and Yale University under Franklin Edgerton. He taught Alex Wayman and Ram Karan Sharma and was appointed professor at UC Berkeley in 1940.

Musashi Tachikawa (born 1942), an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, earned degrees from Nagoya University and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held posts at Nagoya University, National Museum of Ethnology, Graduate University for Advanced Studies, and Aichi Gakuin University.

Muzaffar Alam (born 1947) is a historian and Indologist. After studying at Jamia Millia Islamia, Aligarh Muslim University, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, he held posts at JNU (~1973–2001) and the University of Chicago (~2001), as well as Wisconsin-Madison, Leiden, and Collège de France.

Myles Dillon (1900–1972) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at University College Dublin (~1919–1922). He held academic posts at Trinity College Dublin, University College Dublin, University of Wisconsin-Madison, and the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies (~1949–1972).

Myoshin Fujitake (born 1956) is a Buddhist studies scholar. Fujitake has served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University and was a committee member of the Otani Society (attested 2000).
Mysore Hiriyanna (1871–1950) was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1912–1927) and at the University of Mysore (~1917–1927).

Myōsei Tatsuguchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Diane E. Riggs and Jeff Wilson. Tatsuguchi served at Ryukoku University as a professor (attested 1987) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2015).

Mónika Kiss is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. Kiss pursued doctoral studies in Japanese Studies at Eötvös Loránd University under advisor Masanori Yamaji (attested 2016) and studied under teachers Robert F. Rhodes and Nozomu Saito.
N. Aiyaswami Sastri was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held professorships at Sri Venkateswara Oriental College (attested 1940) and Visva-Bharati University (attested 1971).

N. Veezhinathan is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned a PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University (-1964) under A. Sankaran. After research at Deccan College (1960–1963), he became Lecturer in Sanskrit at University of Madras in 1964, succeeding K. Kunjunni Raja.

N. Venkataramanayya (1891–1976) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Ferrand Edward Corley. He served as Reader of Indian History and Archæology at the University of Madras and Deputy Director for Epigraphy in Andhra Pradesh.

Nagin J. Shah (born 1931) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Acting Director at the L.D. Institute of Indology (attested 1968), where he succeeded Dalsukh D. Malvania, and he taught Maria Heim.

Nalinaksha Dutt (1894–1973) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Chittagong College, the University of Calcutta (PhD), and the University of London (DLitt ~1921–1924), later serving as Head of the Pali Department at Calcutta and teaching Kshanika Saha.

Nalini Balbir (born 1955) is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Colette Caillat (~1976–1980). She has served as a professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1988–2020) and as Directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2000).
